### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The standard treatment protocol for osteoblastic osteosarcoma, particularly in the distal femur of an 18-year-old, typically involves a multimodal approach. This includes neoadjuvant chemotherapy to reduce tumor size, which facilitates limb-salvage surgery. Following surgical resection, adjuvant chemotherapy is administered to minimize the risk of recurrence. This approach is supported by consensus, with studies indicating that neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy is the preferred treatment strategy, achieving success rates around 85-90%. Therefore, the most appropriate option is neoadjuvant chemotherapy followed by surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy.
